results.explanation: At the declared POST /process/text entry, the verified caller is obtained through get_verified_user. The caller-selected collection_name is taken from form_data and, because it is supplied, the route invokes _validate_collection_access with access_type='write' before constructing documents or calling save_docs_to_vector_db. That caller-side validator delegates to the shared filter_accessible_collections policy. For a non-admin and an existing knowledge-base ID, the shared path admits the name only when Knowledges.check_access_by_user_id(..., permission='write') succeeds; otherwise the existing KB is not admitted, and the validator raises HTTP 403. Under the stated premise that the selected existing collection has neither ownership nor an explicit write grant, the authorization check blocks the request, so attacker-selected text does not reach the vector-database write sink.

control.statement: The route-level validator delegates the requested collection set and write access type to filter_accessible_collections, then computes denied names and raises HTTP 403 when any are denied.

citations.quote:
async def _validate_collection_access(collection_names: list[str], user, access_type: str = 'read') -> None:
    """
    Raise 403 if the user lacks access to any of the requested collections.
    Delegates to the shared filter_accessible_collections utility so the
    access rules stay in one place.
    """
    requested = set(collection_names)
    allowed = await filter_accessible_collections(requested, user, access_type=access_type)
    denied = requested - allowed
    if denied:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail=ERROR_MESSAGES.ACCESS_PROHIBITED,
        )
